title: Build OS Agent Session Checkpoint v1
description: A point-in-time description of an agent working session's STATE. It is not a transcript, and it is not canonical project state. Durable Build OS artifacts in GitHub outrank any checkpoint that disagrees with them.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Consumers reject checkpoints whose version they do not understand rather than guessing.

repository.description: GitHub repository this session is working in, as owner/repo.

workstream_id.description: Build OS workstream this session belongs to, when it belongs to one. Null for work that has not been given a workstream yet.

session_id.description: Stable identifier for this session, unchanged across checkpoints. Reusing an id means 'same session'; a new id means 'new session'.

agent.description: Which agent is working. 'human' is legitimate — a person working a session is still a session.

agent_name.description: Optional display name, e.g. a model or tool label. Never used for identity or authorization.

objective.description: One sentence: what this session is trying to accomplish.

status.description: UNKNOWN is deliberately absent: it is a state consumers assign to a silent session, never a state an agent may claim.

phase.description: Build OS workstream phase this session is operating in, when known.

completed.description: Short factual statements of what is done. Not narration, not reasoning.

needs_owner.description: True only when the owner personally must act. An agent waiting on CI is blocked; it does not need the owner.

next_step.description: The single most useful next action, matching the workstream file's Next Step where one exists.

owner_result.description: The terminal owner-facing state this session has reached, when it has reached one. Null or absent while work is still in flight: an in-progress session has no owner result, and 'no result yet' is never SHIP. Derived from durable state — where a durable Build OS artifact disagrees, the artifact wins and the disagreement is surfaced. See framework/OWNER_INTERFACE.md.

related_pr.description: PR this session is currently working on, when there is one. A workstream may span many PRs; a session works one at a time.

updated_at.description: When this checkpoint was produced, RFC 3339. Consumers use it for staleness, so it must be the real time.
